utterances.text: You say that your teams were restricted by special police from entering certain areas. Where were your teams restricted and on what dates?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any details about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Also that sentence discusses special police were cleansing the area ostensibly of Serbian pockets of resistance and clearing mines. From whom did you obtain that information?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was information given to me from the monitors who had met the special police. That was an explanation why couldn't go into a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Which monitors are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNCIVPOL monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any of the names of the UNCIVPOL monitors that may have given this information to you?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall any of them?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few names I could recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give me the names?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an Indonesian guy called Rema Shendran [phoen], Petro Romassev, the Knin station commander, went often out into the area. There was a Swedish female, officer, Lila was the first name I don't remember the last name. We had a few Portuguese, some Irish monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would these reports have been given to you in writing or would they have been given to you verbally? How would they have been given to you?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tellings about restriction of movement which have been told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So there is nothing in writing about this as far as --

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware at all of any -- of these -- so I guess I take it since you haven't been out in the field observing these things, you haven't been able to see what special police operations were all about at that time or what they were for. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You state in your next sentence of your statement: "I never heard any of our teams witness nor have I ever witnessed this so-called Serb resistance." That is something that you received verbally from your teams?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The -- it's fair to state that you never witnessed this so-called Serb resistance because you weren't necessarily up in the hills and the woods and the mountains. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if there was any, you wouldn't have known about it?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you wear on August 28th, we had a witness who came here and testified earlier this week, that there were several -- nine Serbian ARSK soldier who turned themselves in to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, could I try to understand what the last answer of the witness was. You asked him, "It's fair to state that you never witnessed this so-called Serb resistance because you weren't up in the hills, woods or mountains," and then you said "that's correct." Have you considered that an implied suggestion in this question is that Serb resistance did exist in the hills, woods or mountains? Are you aware of whether there was such Serb resistance in the hills, woods or mountains, and at what point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm not aware of any Serb resistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether in woods or mountains or cities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or cities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And cities. Mr. Kuzmanovic, composite questions lead to this kind of confusion, and that doesn't assist the Chamber because there is a suggestion in it which is not observed by the witness, and that's not the first time, even not with this witness, that you get answers which may suit you well but which bring us not specifically further to the truth. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Elleby, is your lack of awareness because of information people told you or was that just what you assume based on what you saw in and around Knin?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. You have told us that you weren't aware in your statement or you have -- "nor have I ever witnessed this so-called Serb resistance."

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You follow me?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see or hear anything myself, and no such incidents were reported to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. By UNCIVPOL?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the UNCIVPOL monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any such incidents were reported to you -- I will re-ask the question. Would the UNMOs report to you about any of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the UNMOs would not report to me, but it would be an issue on the morning meetings with the military in the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that on August 28th which with discussed with a previous witness that nine ARSK soldiers essentially turned themselves in to the special police who, in turn, brought them to the police in Knin, these ARSK soldiers having been in the woods and hills of Sector South?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to state that as far as you're aware -- strike that. The -- what were the badges or the emblems on the uniforms that you saw that you said were -- when you saw the special police. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was some sort of lightening on the badge of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where would that be, on the chest on the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I remember it, on the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the next paragraph of your statement you talk about reported to you by teams of areas which were closed off on the basis of Croatian special police conducting clean-up operations were destroyed. Can you tell me, on what dates or what places these reports came to you?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have that details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, is any -- you had mentioned before that the discussion of witnessing this resistance or not witnessing this Serb resistance was not in writing anywhere. Would any of this information in the last paragraph about the Croatian special police have been provided in writing anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been, but I don't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, the closed-off areas are not in relation to a certain period of time. Could we ask the witness from when to when this happened that teams reported to you that areas were closed off on the basis of Croatian special police conducting clean-up operations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I remember it, it was basically the first two, maybe three weeks after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it is your recollection that, just to make it clear, that this portion of your last paragraph of page 4 of your statement that areas were closed off on the basis of Croatian special police conducting clean-up operations was two -- in the weeks immediately after Operation Storm, two to three weeks, did you say?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you -- do you have a definition for us about what you think clean-up or mop-up operations are, Mr. Elleby?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood it that there could be RSK troops in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of actions would be undertaken during these clean-up or mop-up operations?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So your understanding of what a clean-up or mop-up operation is is that there were RSK soldiers in the area and beyond that you have no idea of what the elements of that mop-up operation would be?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever meet any members of the special police?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How often did you have joint meetings with members of either the UNMOs, the -- strike that. Did you have joint meetings at any time with any UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had a meeting every morning where every branch in the UN were gathered with the general, UN general. And then we had talks before shipping out the Human Rights Watch teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And generally what was discussed in those meetings?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general situation what did it look like, where should we go, what was reported the day before. We only have -- had limited resources, so I think only two or three teams went out every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And two or three teams would be comprised of how many people?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three plus an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Three UNCIVPOL members plus an interpreter would be a team?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. One UNCIVPOL member, an UNMO, UNHCR and then an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you'd have three vehicles to cover all of Sector South?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And would those vehicles go out in the morning and then come back at 4.00 or 5.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went out in the morning but they were back very late. As it got darker and darker as the time went on, we had to make the patrols shorter. Because of security I wanted them to be back in daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Had you ever gone out on any of these patrols?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The -- sorry. As far as UNCIVPOL reporting, can you tell me, Mr. Elleby, was it the practice of UNCIVPOL members when they came upon a crime to remove -- for example if there was a dead body to remove the body or to photograph the body. Give us an estimation of what you would do when you came upon a crime that you observed? And by you, I mean UNCIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. UNCIVPOL members would only observe and take notes. We were not supposed to touch bodies and we were not allowed to take any pictures and we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Why weren't you allowed to take any pictures?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not allowed from the Croatian police. We wanted that permission but we never got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There were, pictures however, taken that we have received throughout the course of this trial so far of various sightings, were there not, where people were killed; do you know?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But essentially it was the practice of UNCIVPOL not to do anything to the crime scene but to leave it the way it is?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were those instructions reported to people who were at the scene, moaning any civilians that might be there or anyone else that might be in the area to leave the scene as it is and not to disturb a potential crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a policy of UNCIVPOLs to tell people don't touch the crime scene, leave it as it is, wait until the investigating people get there?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's general way of thinking when you're a police officer, but it was never written down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the practice as you mentioned not to disturb the crime scene, was that somewhere in any written form that UNCIVPOL had?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any written guidelines that UNCIVPOL had as to dealing with crime scenes in general?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was from HQ in Zagreb a standard operation procedures, I remember that in detail. It could very well have been included here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that something that -- obviously you said you haven't seen that in who knows how long. You thought it did exist?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did exist and several page there is was also something we called code of conduct, and these two -- these two compilation could very well have included what you're asking here, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you have -- what were the procedures then be when you came across a crime scene, for example, where someone had been killed, what would the next step that UNCIVPOL -- what was the next step that UNCIVPOL would take?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be to report it to the Croatian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And depending upon where you were, would you always report it to Knin?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If it was CIVPOL patrol, from Gracac, for example they would go to that station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it would depend on where the CIVPOL patrol came from?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then that CIVPOL patrol would report to, as you said, in Gracac or Knin or whatever other town had a police station?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go to P238, please. P238 is dated August 26th 1995. There's a question that I wanted to ask you about this follow-up report, Mr. Elleby. It says: "On 26.8.1995 Knin CIVPOL informed Croatian policija of --" I think that must be arson, it's blocked out there -- "and murder cases committed by Croatian special forces in hamlet Grubori of Plavno village. Now, this is the day after the occurrence of this incident and yet there's a conclusion made that the Croatian police forces in this hamlet have committed this crime. Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, again, I'm not sure we are looking at the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It could be the -- well, mine is 238, 65 ter 1320. If that is not P238, I apologise. According to my document that I received from the registrar, 1320 is P238. Do you have it, Ms. Frolich?

utterances.speaker: MS. FROLICH
utterances.text: 1320 is the P238, but -- and that is the ERN number that is being shown on screen, but unless I'm very much mistaken, but the document being shown on screen is not the document that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- let me give you the ERN number. This is how it came to me in the dossier, so it's R090-3292, it appears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the one on the screen is 3275.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could pull up 3292. It's P237, I have been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see it, Mr. Elleby?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you've forgotten my question, but ... Do you recall my question?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I cannot explain why Mr. Romassev wrote this about -- that it should be committed by Croatian special forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It seems to be, at least as of the date of this document, somewhat of a rush to judgement, don't you think?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It also notes that later in this document that HRS representatives of Croatian military command attended the scene, promised to take necessary action, help bury the dead bodies and sanitize the area? HRS, do you know what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Knin CIVPOL appears to have reported this on the first line to the Croatian police. Do you know which station that would have been reported to?

utterances.speaker: JAN ELLEBY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Typically that would have been report to the Knin police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you give me one second, Mr. Kuzmanovic, to read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Mr. Kuzmanovic, I'm looking at the clock, we have to finish for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour, I'll tell you if I'm done or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm done. So I just wanted to check with co-counsel and make sure that we didn't have to start with me again tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, would have been a pleasure to listen to you tomorrow morning as well, Mr. Kuzmanovic, so don't be too shy in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's good to know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is valid for all Defence counsel. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, and if Mr. Registrar, could help us out as -- in which courtroom. In this same courtroom, number I. Mr. Elleby, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00. You will then be cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe, who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. I'd like to instruct you again that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, testimony already given or testimony still to be given. We stand adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of May, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
